reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge.* Reviewed `http-retries` (`b04b610`) against `main` (`5f9be03`). Four findings:

1. *High — `timeoutMs: 0` no longer disables timeouts.* `src/http.js:11` uses `||`, replacing zero with 10,000. The nightly export explicitly passes zero (`src/export.js:4`), so exports taking over 10 seconds to receive response headers now abort.
   *Fix:* Restore `??` and add a zero-timeout regression test.

2. *High — retries can duplicate non-idempotent operations.* `src/http.js:30–33` retries regardless of HTTP method. A POST that commits work but returns 503 will be submitted again, potentially three times by default. I verified the same POST body is sent twice after a 503.
   *Fix:* Default to retry-safe methods; require explicit opt-in or an idempotency guarantee for other operations.

3. *Medium — discarded response bodies aren’t released.* `src/http.js:31–33` starts another attempt without consuming or cancelling the previous response body. With native fetch, unread error bodies can retain connections and exhaust the pool under sustained failures.
   *Fix:* Cancel or drain each discarded response before retrying, with coverage using a real response body.

4. *Medium — retries ignore `Retry-After`.* `src/http.js:33` only uses local jitter, even when a 429/503 tells clients to wait. Default waits are under 250ms and 500ms, which can burn all attempts while the upstream is still rate-limiting.
   *Fix:* Honor valid `Retry-After` values, with an explicit maximum-wait policy.

*Validation:* All 3 existing tests pass. Read-only probes confirmed the zero-timeout regression, repeated POST, missing body cancellation, and ignored `Retry-After`. No repository files were changed.
